I’m getting the specific eligibility provisions in Section 2.1.2 and checking for any change notices that amend Policy 3K-2.## General CAP/DA eligibility criteria under NC Medicaid

Under **NC Medicaid Clinical Coverage Policy 3K-2 (Community Alternatives Program for Disabled Adults (CAP/DA))**, a person generally must meet **both Medicaid eligibility requirements and CAP/DA-specific waiver criteria**.

### 1. Must be enrolled in NC Medicaid
The policy states:

### 2. Must be in one of the listed Medicaid aid programs
The CAP/DA policy lists these Medicaid eligibility categories:

- **Medicaid to the Aged (MAA)**
- **Medicaid to the Blind (MAB)**
- **Medicaid to the Disabled (MAD)**
- **Health Care for Workers with Disabilities (HCWD)**

**Citation:** Policy **3K-2**, Section **sec:doc:clinical_policy:3K-2:_s18** (“b. Medicaid Eligibility Requirements”).  
**Effective date:** **2025-09-01**.  
**Amendments:** none returned.

**Citation:** Policy **3K-2**, Section **sec:doc:clinical_policy:3K-2:_s17** (“a. Medicaid”).  
**Effective date:** **2025-09-01**.  
**Amendments:** none returned.

### 4. Must be age 18 or older
The CAP/DA policy says the beneficiary:

- “**is age 18 years old and older**.”

**Citation:** Policy **3K-2**, Section **sec:doc:clinical_policy:3K-2:_s17**.  
**Effective date:** **2025-09-01**.  
**Amendments:** none returned.

### 5. Must need a nursing-facility level of care

  **Citation:** Policy **3K-2**, Section **sec:doc:clinical_policy:3K-2:3.2.1**

### 6. Must be part of the waiver’s target group

### 7. Must show need for at least one CAP/DA waiver service

**Citation:** Policy **3K-2**, Section **sec:doc:clinical_policy:3K-2:3.2.1**.  
**Effective date:** **2025-09-01**.  
**Amendments:** none returned.

### 8. Must have an approved/signed service plan
The policy requires the person to:

- “**Have a signed service plan that authorizes one or more waiver services to be rendered on a monthly basis**...”

It also requires, for participation, an approved service plan identifying the amount, duration, frequency, and NPI of services.

**Citation:** Policy **3K-2**, Section **sec:doc:clinical_policy:3K-2:3.2.1**.  
**Effective date:** **2025-09-01**.  
**Amendments:** none returned.

### 9. Must be able to remain safely at home or another approved location with supports
The policy says the beneficiary must be:

- “**Able to maintain health, safety and well-being at their primary private residence or an approved location with the use of both formal and informal supports**”

A nearly identical requirement also appears in the Medicaid subsection.  
**Citations:**  
- Policy **3K-2**, Section **sec:doc:clinical_policy:3K-2:3.2.1**  
- Policy **3K-2**, Section **sec:doc:clinical_policy:3K-2:_s17**

### 10. Must fit within CAP/DA cost limits
Section 3.2.1 requires:

- “**Paid care needs can be maintained within the average institutional cost of the CAP/DA waiver**.”

**Citation:** Policy **3K-2**, Section **sec:doc:clinical_policy:3K-2:3.2.1**.  
**Effective date:** **2025-09-01**.  
**Amendments:** none returned.

### 11. Must have a primary physician and emergency backup plan
The policy also requires that the beneficiary:

- “**Has a primary physician that can link and coordinate all medical services**”; and
- “**Has an emergency back-up and disaster plan**” specifying who will provide care if direct care staff or the primary caregiver cannot.

**Citation:** Policy **3K-2**, Section **sec:doc:clinical_policy:3K-2:3.2.1**.  
**Effective date:** **2025-09-01**.  
**Amendments:** none returned.

### 12. Must choose CAP/DA and have a waiver slot
The policy says the beneficiary:

- “**exercises freedom of choice by choosing to enter the waiver or maintain enrollment in the waiver**...”

- **individualized, specific, and consistent** with the symptoms or confirmed diagnosis, and **not in excess of the beneficiary’s needs**;

- they are **ordered by a physician, physician assistant, or nurse practitioner**;

- there has been a **documented face-to-face encounter** with the beneficiary and the ordering physician/PA/NP **no more than six months before** initiation of orthotics/prosthetics;
- the beneficiary’s need is **reviewed at least annually** by the ordering physician/PA/NP.

That same section also states:

- **Orthotic devices** are medically necessary when required to **correct or prevent skeletal deformities**, **support or align movable body parts**, or **preserve or improve physical function**.

  - a **reasonable and medically necessary part of the treatment plan**;
  - **consistent with the diagnosis and medical condition**, especially functional limitations and symptoms; and
  - **of high quality**, with **replacement parts available and obtainable**.

- **Devices for the beneficiary’s comfort or convenience** or for the convenience of the beneficiary’s caregiver(s);
- **Backup devices** or **duplicates** kept available at different locations;
- **Devices and supplies for residents of nursing facilities**;
- **Devices or supplies covered by another agency**; and
- **Equipment or supplies for beneficiaries receiving hospice care**, as defined in Subsection 7.3.

In addition, under **CCP 5B, Section `sec:doc:clinical_policy:5B:4.1` (Policy 5B, §4.1)**, Medicaid will not cover a service/item when:

- the beneficiary does **not meet eligibility requirements** in Section 2.0;
- the beneficiary does **not meet the criteria** in Section 3.0;

- the item/service is **experimental, investigational, or part of a clinical trial**.

- **ordered by an authorized clinician**,
- **medically necessary**,
- tied to the person’s **diagnosis and functional needs**,
- supported by a **recent face-to-face visit**,
- and **not just for convenience, backup, or duplication**.

- covered by **another agency**,

The relevant policy is **Clinical Coverage Policy 8C, Outpatient Behavioral Health Services Provided by Direct-Enrolled Providers**. The current authoritative document is **Policy 8C**, effective **April 15, 2025**, and **no amendments were returned** by the amendment lookup.  
Citations below are to the specific sections of **Policy 8C**.

### 1) Entrance criteria
A beneficiary meets the **entrance criteria** for outpatient behavioral health services if the following are present:

- **A current DSM-5 diagnosis**;
- **Behavioral, psychological, or biological dysfunction and functional impairment** consistent with and associated with that diagnosis;
- If a **higher level of care is indicated but unavailable**, or the beneficiary is **refusing** that higher level of care, **outpatient services can be provided until the appropriate level of care is available or to support the beneficiary to participate in that higher level of care**;
- The beneficiary is **capable of developing skills** to manage symptoms, make behavioral changes, and respond favorably to therapeutic interventions; and
- There is **no evidence that alternative interventions would be more effective**, based on North Carolina community practice standards.  
  **Citation:** Policy **8C**, **Section sec:doc:clinical_policy:8C:3.2.1.1** (“3.2.1.1 Entrance Criteria”), effective **2025-04-15**, no amendments found.

### 2) Continued service criteria
For **continued services**, the policy requires:

- **Any one** of the following:
  - The desired outcome or level of functioning has **not been restored, improved, or sustained** over the timeframe in the treatment plan;
  - The beneficiary **continues to be at risk for relapse** based on current clinical assessment and history; **or**
  - There is a **tenuous nature of the functional gains**;

**And**, in addition to the above, **any one** of the following:
- The beneficiary has **achieved current treatment plan goals**, and **additional goals are indicated** as evidenced by documented symptoms; **or**
- The beneficiary is **making satisfactory progress toward meeting goals** and there is documentation supporting that.  
  **Citation:** Policy **8C**, **Section sec:doc:clinical_policy:8C:3.2.1.2** (“3.2.1.2 Continued Service Criteria”), effective **2025-04-15**, no amendments found.

### 3) Discharge criteria
A beneficiary meets **discharge criteria** if:

- The beneficiary’s **level of functioning has improved** with respect to the goals in the treatment plan;
- The beneficiary or legally responsible person **no longer wishes to receive services**; **or**
- The beneficiary, based on presentation and **failure to show improvement despite modifications in the treatment plan**, requires a **more appropriate best practice or evidence-based treatment modality** based on North Carolina community practice standards.  
  **Citation:** Policy **8C**, **Section sec:doc:clinical_policy:8C:3.2.1.3** (“3.2.1.3 Discharge Criteria”), effective **2025-04-15**, no amendments found.

## Practical takeaway
In plain language:

- **To start services**, the person needs a current DSM diagnosis, related functional impairment, capacity to benefit from outpatient treatment, and no better alternative intervention.
- **To stay in services**, there must still be clinical need or relapse risk, plus either new goals or documented progress toward goals.
- **To discharge**, either goals have been met enough to improve functioning, the person wants to stop, or outpatient treatment is no longer the right modality.

per_question.question: Does NC Medicaid cover Personal Care Services for beneficiaries who live in an assisted living facility?

## Which policy applies
The relevant policy is **Clinical Coverage Policy 3L-1, “State Plan Personal Care Services (PCS) Provided in Congregate Settings.”**  
This is the correct policy for **assisted living / adult care home-type settings**. I am **not** using CCP 3L as the primary source, because **3L-1** specifically applies to **congregate settings**, while 3L is a different PCS policy.  
Citation: **Policy 3L-1, Section sec:doc:clinical_policy:3L-1:3.2.1**.

## What settings are included
Under **Policy 3L-1, Section sec:doc:clinical_policy:3L-1:3.2.1**, the beneficiary must reside in:

- “**a congregate facility licensed by the State of North Carolina as an Adult Care Home (ACH)** ...”
- or a qualifying licensed group home.

That section also says providers may be:
- “**a congregate facility licensed by the State of North Carolina as an Adult Care Home** ...”  
Citation: **Policy 3L-1, Section sec:doc:clinical_policy:3L-1:6.1**.

In plain language: if the person lives in a **licensed Adult Care Home**, that is the category most commonly associated with **assisted living-type facilities**, PCS can be covered **if all other criteria are met**.

## Key eligibility criteria
Under **Policy 3L-1, Section sec:doc:clinical_policy:3L-1:3.2.1**, the beneficiary must, among other things:

- have a **medical or mental condition, disability, or cognitive impairment**; and
- demonstrate unmet needs for at least:
  - **three of five qualifying ADLs with limited hands-on assistance**, or
  - **two ADLs, one requiring extensive assistance**, or
  - **two ADLs, one requiring full dependence**.

That same section also requires that:

- the setting be safe and inspected,
- **no other third-party payer** be responsible for PCS,
- **no family/household member or other informal caregiver** be available, willing, and able to provide the authorized services during the times PCS is provided,
- the services be directly linked to the documented condition/impairment,
- the beneficiary be under the ongoing direct care of a physician, and
- the beneficiary be **medically stable** and **not require continuous care, monitoring, or supervision by a licensed nurse or other licensed health professional**.  
Citation: **Policy 3L-1, Section sec:doc:clinical_policy:3L-1:3.2.1**.

## Important exclusions
Even when PCS is approved in an assisted living/adult care home setting, NC Medicaid does **not** cover certain services under this PCS policy.  
**Policy 3L-1, Section sec:doc:clinical_policy:3L-1:4.2.1.2** says Medicaid does **not** cover, among other things:

- skilled nursing services by an LPN or RN,
- services by other licensed health professionals,
- respite care,
- transportation,
- errands,
- companion sitting/leisure activities,
- ongoing supervision/monitoring,
- and **room and board**.

That means **living in the facility itself is not what Medicaid PCS covers**; Medicaid may cover the **personal care service component**, but **not room and board**.  
Citation: **Policy 3L-1, Section sec:doc:clinical_policy:3L-1:4.2.1.2**.

## When PCS would not be covered in the facility

I’m going to pull the staff qualification sections too, because the certification requirements explicitly depend on the provider using qualified case managers and supervisors.## NC Medicaid HIV case management provider certification and decertification

The governing source is **Clinical Coverage Policy 12B, Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) Case Management**. The current document returned by NC Medicaid’s policy database is **Policy 12B**, effective **2020-01-15**, and **no amendments were returned** by the amendment tool, so this appears to be the current authoritative document.  
**Citations:** Policy 12B, Sections **6.2.1**, **6.2.4**, **6.2.5**, effective **2020-01-15**; no amendments returned for document **doc:clinical_policy:12B**.

### 1) Certification requirements

Under **Policy 12B, Section sec:doc:clinical_policy:12B:6.2.1 (Section 6.2.1, “Certification Requirements”)**, an HIV case management provider must:

- Have a **documented successful record of three (3) years of providing or managing HIV Case Management programs**.
- Ensure services are provided by **qualified case managers** meeting **Sections 6.1.1, 6.1.2, and 6.1.3**.
- Ensure supervision by **qualified supervisors** meeting **Sections 6.1.4 and 6.1.5**.
- **Enroll each physical site** with NC Medicaid as a provider of HIV Case Management services.
- Meet **applicable state and federal laws** governing Medicaid participation.
- **Maintain certification** as a qualified HIV Case Management provider.
- Demonstrate compliance with **initial and ongoing certification processes**.
- Demonstrate compliance with **monitoring and evaluation of case management records through a quality improvement plan**.
- Allow **NC Medicaid or its designated contractor** to review beneficiary records and inspect agency operation and financial records.
- Notify NC Medicaid or its contractor of proposed changes such as **owner/name/address/phone/business dissolution** within **30 calendar days of the proposed change** and no later than **5 business days after the actual change**.
- **Within one year of enrollment with Medicaid as a provider**, achieve **national accreditation** from one of the designated accrediting agencies:
  - ACHC
  - CARF
  - CHAP
  - COA
  - PHAB
  - The Joint Commission
  - URAC

**Citation:** Policy 12B, **Section sec:doc:clinical_policy:12B:6.2.1**.

### 2) Staff qualification requirements tied to certification

Because Section 6.2.1 requires the provider to use qualified staff, the following sections are part of the certification picture:

#### HIV case managers
Under **Section sec:doc:clinical_policy:12B:6.1.1**, a case manager must meet one of the listed education/licensure pathways, including for example:

- Master’s degree in a human services field; or
- Bachelor’s degree in social work; or
- Bachelor’s degree in a human services field/related curriculum with at least **15 semester hours** in social work, counseling, or public health and **6 months** of relevant experience; or
- Bachelor’s degree plus **1 year** of relevant counseling/human services experience; or
- Relevant NC licensure (RN, NP, physician, PA, or certified substance abuse counselor) plus **2 years** of human services experience.

**Citation:** Policy 12B, **Section sec:doc:clinical_policy:12B:6.1.1**.

#### Case management competencies
Under **Section sec:doc:clinical_policy:12B:6.1.2**, case managers must be able to perform assessment, develop beneficiary-centered goals, provide referral/linkage, monitor care and services, and document and attest to accuracy by signature.

**Citation:** Policy 12B, **Section sec:doc:clinical_policy:12B:6.1.2**.

#### Knowledge, skills, and abilities
Under **Section sec:doc:clinical_policy:12B:6.1.3**, case managers must have documented HIV knowledge within **one year of hire**, including transmission, treatment, medications, and barriers to compliance, plus communication, assessment, documentation, cultural sensitivity, prioritization, and related skills.

**Citation:** Policy 12B, **Section sec:doc:clinical_policy:12B:6.1.3**.

#### Supervisors
Under **Section sec:doc:clinical_policy:12B:6.1.4**, supervisors must meet one of the listed education/licensure and experience pathways. Under **Section sec:doc:clinical_policy:12B:6.1.5**, they must be able to direct and evaluate services, understand case management principles, conduct analytical evaluations, and apply knowledge of federal and state assistance programs for the HIV-positive population.

**Citations:** Policy 12B, **Sections sec:doc:clinical_policy:12B:6.1.4** and **sec:doc:clinical_policy:12B:6.1.5**.

#### Training
Training also matters because failure to complete it can lead to decertification. The policy states:

- Basic training for case managers and supervisors must cover the items listed in **Section 6.1.7.1**.
- Annual training in **Section 6.1.7.2** includes confidentiality, cultural competency, current HIV disease management trends, ethics, refresher core components, and treatment of individuals who are HIV positive.
- **Six hours of the twelve hour annual requirement must include clinically oriented training.**

**Citations:** Policy 12B, **Sections sec:doc:clinical_policy:12B:6.1.7.1** and **sec:doc:clinical_policy:12B:6.1.7.2**.

### 3) Recertification requirements

Under **Section sec:doc:clinical_policy:12B:6.2.4 (Section 6.2.4, “Recertification”)**, the provider must:

- Submit a **complete and signed Recertification Application** to NC Medicaid or its designated contractor **within 60 calendar days of receipt**;
- Submit copies of all items in **Section 6.2.3** that changed since initial certification;
- Submit copies of all HIV case manager and supervisor credentials;
- Submit annual summary or summaries of **quality improvement activities**, including **outcome metrics**; and
- Submit to an **on-site recertification visit**, including review of beneficiary records or other clinical/business documentation as needed.

**Citation:** Policy 12B, **Section sec:doc:clinical_policy:12B:6.2.4**.

### 4) When can a provider be decertified?

Under **Section sec:doc:clinical_policy:12B:6.2.5 (Section 6.2.5, “Decertification”)**, an HIV case management provider may be decertified for any of the following:

- **Failure to provide core service components**
- **Fraudulent billing practices**
- **Owner(s) being convicted of a felony charge**
- **Failure to develop, submit, and implement a written plan of correction** to resolve unmet program requirements cited by NC Medicaid or its contractor, or failure to make recommended corrections, **within 30 calendar days**
- **Falsification of records**
- **Violation of a beneficiary’s confidentiality**
- **Employment of staff who do not meet the criteria** in Section 6.1
- **Failure of staff to complete mandatory basic training within 90 days of employment**
- **Failure of staff to obtain required CEUs** as specified in Section 6.1
- **Failure to provide staff supervision** adequate to meet beneficiaries’ needs
- **Failure to submit required documentation** within the required time frames
- **Failure to provide documentation sufficient to support billing**, as specified in Section 7.5
- **Failure to implement and enforce a quality improvement program**
- **Failure to timely notify NC Medicaid** or its contractor about changes in agency name, director/ownership, mailing address, or phone number, causing inability to contact the provider
- **Failure to comply with applicable federal and state laws, regulations, state reimbursement plan, and Medicaid policies**
- **Failure to enroll any beneficiaries within four months of certification**
- **Failure to achieve or maintain certification requirements** under Section 6.2

**Citation:** Policy 12B, **Section sec:doc:clinical_policy:12B:6.2.5**.

## Plain-language summary

To be certified, an HIV case management provider must have a **3-year successful HIV CM track record**, use **qualified case managers and supervisors**, enroll **each physical site** with Medicaid, maintain a **quality improvement plan**, cooperate with record and financial review, **report business changes on time**, and obtain **national accreditation within one year of Medicaid enrollment**.

A provider can be decertified for **program failures**, **fraud or falsification**, **confidentiality violations**, **using unqualified or untrained staff**, **missing required documentation**, **failing to correct deficiencies**, **not maintaining quality improvement**, **not keeping Medicaid informed of agency changes**, **not complying with law/policy**, **not enrolling beneficiaries within four months**, or otherwise **failing to maintain certification standards**.
